value: Results from the cortical thickness analyses indicated no significant differences in a priori (ventromedial or lateral PFC) or other cortical regions between AUDs+TBI and AUDs alone following appropriate corrections for false positives. There were no groupwise differences in hippocampi, basal ganglia, thalami, or cerebellar volumes following false-positive correction. Secondary analyses were also not significant for overall gray matter or white matter volumes.

The current study did not observe significant differences in cortical thickness, subcortical volumes, or cerebellar volumes between AUDs+TBI relative to AUDs alone, with small effect sizes that were generally bidirectional.

spans.text: Results from the cortical thickness analyses indicated no significant differences in a priori (ventromedial or lateral PFC) or other cortical regions between AUDs+TBI and AUDs alone following appropriate corrections for false positives. A cortical representation of effects sizes (Cohen’s d ) indicated small to moderate effects of group across all cortical regions ( ). There were no significant differences in estimated total intracranial volume between groups ( p > .10). A series of analyses of covariance indicated no groupwise differences in hippocampi, basal ganglia, thalami, or cerebellar volumes following false-positive correction, with all effect sizes in the small range (all p > .10; Cohen’s d range, −0.22 to 0.09). Secondary analyses were also not significant for the main effect of group (both p > .10) for overall gray matter (Cohen’s d = −0.07) or white matter (Cohen’s d = −0.23) volumes.
